text: Which keyword in Java is used to inherit from a superclass?
explanation: The 'extends' keyword establishes class inheritance in Java.

text: What is the default value of a boolean field in a Java class?
explanation: Primitive boolean class fields default to false.

text: Which concept allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method defined in its superclass?
explanation: Method overriding occurs when a subclass re-declares an instance method with identical signature.

text: Which Java collection interface guarantees that elements are stored without duplicates?
explanation: Set is a collection that cannot contain duplicate elements.

text: What does the 'final' keyword on a variable in Java indicate?
optionB: The value cannot be reassigned once initialized
optionC: The variable cannot be accessed outside package
optionD: The variable is destroyed at end of method
explanation: A final variable's reference or value cannot be modified once set.

text: Which OOP pillar is achieved through private fields and public getters/setters?
explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and restrains direct external access.

text: Which memory area in the JVM stores dynamically created objects?
explanation: The Heap is the runtime data area from which memory for all class instances is allocated.

text: What is the time complexity of looking up a key in a well-balanced HashMap?
explanation: Average case time complexity for HashMap get() and put() is O(1).

text: Which interface must a Java class implement to enable thread execution via Thread class?
explanation: Runnable contains the run() method executed by a Thread.

text: Which of the following is NOT a primitive data type in Java?
explanation: String is an immutable class reference type in java.lang.

text: What happens if an exception is thrown in a try block and caught in a catch block?
optionB: The code in finally block executes, then execution continues
explanation: The finally block always executes regardless of exception handling.

text: Which design pattern ensures that a class has only one instance throughout the entire application?
explanation: Singleton restricts instantiation to a single unique object.

text: What is the purpose of the 'super' keyword in Java?
optionA: To refer to the parent class object or constructor
explanation: super refers directly to the immediate superclass members or constructor.

text: Can an abstract class in Java have constructors?
optionA: No, because it cannot be instantiated directly
optionB: Yes, invoked when subclass constructors execute
optionC: Only if it has no abstract methods
explanation: Abstract classes have constructors to initialize fields when a subclass is instantiated.

text: Which functional interface in java.util.function takes one argument and returns a boolean?
explanation: Predicate<T> defines test(T t) returning boolean.

text: What is autoboxing in Java?
optionB: Automatic conversion between primitive types and their wrapper classes
explanation: Autoboxing converts e.g. int to Integer automatically.

text: What is the difference between '==' and '.equals()' when comparing two Java String objects?
optionA: '==' compares memory references, while '.equals()' compares character contents
optionB: They are identical in all cases
explanation: '==' checks reference equality whereas equals() compares contents.

text: What does the 'transient' keyword in Java do during serialization?
optionB: Marks a field to NOT be serialized
optionD: Writes the field to disk first
explanation: transient fields are skipped during Java object serialization.

text: What is polymorphism in Java?
optionA: Writing code that compiles on any OS
optionB: The ability of an object to take on many forms
explanation: Polymorphism allows subclasses to define distinct behaviors through a shared parent type.

text: Which method is called by the Garbage Collector before an object is reclaimed in older Java versions?
explanation: finalize() was invoked prior to garbage collection.

text: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing IP packets across different networks?
explanation: Layer 3 (Network Layer) handles logical addressing and packet routing.

text: Which port is the default standard for unencrypted HTTP web traffic?
explanation: Port 80 is standard HTTP, while 443 is HTTPS.

text: What protocol is used to automatically assign IP addresses to devices on a local network?
explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) assigns dynamic IP leases.

text: What is the primary difference between TCP and UDP transport protocols?
optionA: UDP is connection-oriented, TCP is connectionless
optionB: TCP guarantees packet delivery with handshakes, while UDP is faster and connectionless
optionC: TCP is only for local networks
explanation: TCP ensures reliable ordered delivery; UDP prioritizes low latency without handshakes.

text: What does DNS stand for in computer networking?
explanation: Domain Name System maps human-readable domain names to numeric IP addresses.

text: Which command line utility tests network connectivity by sending ICMP echo requests?
explanation: ping sends ICMP Echo Request packets to test remote host reachability.

text: What is the default subnet mask for a Class C IPv4 address?
explanation: Class C addresses (/24) use 255.255.255.0 subnet mask.

text: What protocol resolves an IP address to a physical MAC address on a local area network?
explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) translates IPv4 addresses into MAC addresses.

text: What does NAT stand for in router networking?
explanation: NAT allows multiple private devices to share a single public IP address.

text: Which HTTP status code indicates that a requested resource was not found on the server?
explanation: 404 Not Found indicates the requested URL could not be located.

text: What is the length in bits of an IPv6 address?
explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses compared to 32 bits in IPv4.

text: Which layer in the OSI model is responsible for encryption and data compression?
explanation: Layer 6 (Presentation) formats, compresses, and encrypts data.

text: What is a three-way handshake in TCP connection establishment?
explanation: TCP uses SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK to synchronize sequence numbers.

text: Which network topology connects every node directly to a central switch or hub?
explanation: Star topology connects all peripheral nodes to a central hub/switch.

text: What does TTL (Time to Live) in an IP packet header prevent?
optionB: Packets looping indefinitely in network loops
explanation: TTL decrements at each hop; when 0, the packet is discarded.

text: Which protocol is used to retrieve emails from a server while keeping them synchronized across devices?
explanation: IMAP synchronizes mailbox state across multiple client devices.

text: What is the maximum data payload size in a standard Ethernet frame (MTU)?
explanation: Standard Ethernet Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) is 1500 bytes.

text: What port is typically used for secure SSH remote access?
explanation: Port 22 is standard for Secure Shell (SSH) connections.

text: What is the private IPv4 loopback address representing localhost?
explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the standard loopback IP address.

text: Which device operates at Layer 2 to filter and forward frames based on MAC addresses?
explanation: Layer 2 network switches learn MAC addresses and forward frames accordingly.

text: What does the 'A' represent in an RGBA color model?
explanation: Alpha channel defines pixel transparency/opacity from 0.0 to 1.0.

text: What is the standard digital audio sample rate used for CD-quality audio?
explanation: 44.1 kHz is standard CD audio sampling rate.

text: Which image format uses mathematical vectors rather than fixed pixel grids, allowing lossless scaling?
explanation: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scale losslessly without pixelation.

text: What graphical technique smooths jagged stair-step edges along geometric lines and curves?
explanation: Anti-aliasing blends edge pixels with background color to smooth edges.

text: What is the refresh rate of a display that updates its frame buffer 60 times per second?
explanation: 60 frames per second equals a 60 Hz display refresh rate.

text: What audio file format provides raw, uncompressed PCM waveform data?
explanation: WAV is a standard uncompressed audio container format.

text: In computer animation, what is the term for generating intermediate frames between two keyframes?
explanation: Tweening calculates visual transitions between keyframes.

text: Which color space is subtractive and primarily used in professional color printing?
explanation: CMYK (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Key/Black) is subtractive for print inks.

text: What UI principle dictates that interactive UI elements should visually invite their intended action?
explanation: Affordance is the property of an element indicating how it should be used.

text: What component in modern graphics pipelines calculates per-pixel lighting and color on screen?
explanation: Fragment/Pixel shaders compute color and lighting per rendered fragment.

text: Which lossless image compression format supports 8-bit alpha channel transparency?
explanation: PNG-24/32 supports full 8-bit alpha transparency.

text: What audio term describes the perceptible time delay between audio generation and output playback?
explanation: Audio latency is the delay between input trigger and audible output.

text: In 2D game engines, what coordinate system origin (0, 0) is standard for canvas rendering?
explanation: Screen and canvas graphics coordinates place (0, 0) at the top-left.

text: What technique avoids visual screen tearing by synchronizing frame rendering with display refresh cycles?
explanation: V-Sync synchronizes GPU frame presentation with monitor vertical refreshes.

text: What is the bit depth required to represent True Color (16.7 million colors)?
explanation: 24-bit color allocates 8 bits each to Red, Green, and Blue channels.

text: What is spatial audio rendering in horror game sound design?
optionA: Playing music louder in big rooms
optionB: Simulating sound distance, azimuth, and room reverberation relative to the player's ears
explanation: Spatial audio positions sound sources 3-dimensionally in virtual space.

text: What musical term describes notes played with sudden, sharp detachment?
explanation: Staccato indicates brief, detached, sharp articulation of notes.

text: What is an Atlas or Sprite Sheet in 2D game rendering?
optionB: A single large image containing multiple smaller sub-textures to minimize GPU draw calls
explanation: Sprite sheets pack multiple character frames into one texture to optimize rendering.

text: What audio phenomenon creates artificial acoustic reflection simulating large empty halls?
explanation: Reverb simulates persistent reflections of sound waves in physical enclosures.

text: Which image resolution corresponds to Full HD standard?
explanation: Full High Definition is 1920x1080 pixels at 16:9 aspect ratio.

text: Which great Khmer King built the iconic temple of Angkor Wat in the early 12th century?
explanation: Angkor Wat was commissioned by King Suryavarman II as a Hindu temple for Vishnu.

text: Which monarch built the Bayon temple, famous for its serene, smiling stone faces?
explanation: King Jayavarman VII built the Bayon temple at the center of Angkor Thom.

text: What historic script is the Khmer writing system historically derived from?
explanation: Khmer script evolved from Southern Indian Pallava script, rooted in ancient Brahmi.

text: What great freshwater lake in Cambodia was the lifeblood and fishery of the Angkor Empire?
explanation: Tonle Sap Lake provided vital water, silt, and fish supporting Angkor's population.

text: What ancient material was historically used in Cambodia to write sacred Buddhist and royal scriptures?
explanation: Trai (palm-leaf manuscripts) preserved Buddhist scriptures and ancient chronicles.

text: What famous architectural feature was used in Angkor to store vast water reserves for agriculture?
explanation: The West and East Barays were colossal engineered reservoirs measuring up to 8 km long.

text: Which mythical multi-headed serpent features prominently as balustrades in Khmer architecture?
explanation: The multi-headed Naga serpent symbolizes protection and bridges between realms.

text: What was the capital city established by King Jayavarman VII after liberating Angkor from the Chams?
explanation: Angkor Thom was the fortified royal capital founded by Jayavarman VII.

text: Which temple is renowned for being enveloped by colossal banyan and silk-cotton tree roots?
explanation: Ta Prohm was left largely in its natural, jungle-entwined state as found.

text: What pink sandstone temple is famed for its exquisite, intricate miniature stone carvings?
explanation: Banteay Srei (Citadel of Women) features exceptionally delicate pink sandstone reliefs.

text: In Khmer classical mythology, what creature represents the sun eagle and traditional mount of Vishnu?
explanation: Garuda is the mythical divine avian mount of Lord Vishnu.

text: What historical event is depicted in the famous 49-meter bas-relief gallery at Angkor Wat?
optionB: Churning of the Ocean of Milk (Samudra Manthan)
explanation: The Churning of the Ocean of Milk depicts gods and asuras pulling the serpent Vasuki.

text: What sacred mountain north of Siem Reap served as the sacred quarry for Angkorian sandstones?
explanation: Phnom Kulen was the quarry source and birthplace of the Khmer Empire under Jayavarman II in 802 AD.

text: Which traditional Khmer shadow puppet theater art is recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage?
explanation: Sbek Thom is the sacred ancient shadow puppet theater utilizing cowhide figures.

text: What is the traditional woven silk or cotton scarf that is a national symbol of Cambodian identity?
explanation: The Krama is the iconic multipurpose woven gingham scarf of Cambodia.

text: What traditional Khmer martial art features ancient hand-to-hand and weapon combat carved on temple walls?
explanation: Kun Bokator dates back over a thousand years and is depicted on Angkor bas-reliefs.

text: What classical Khmer architectural sanctuary style sits atop a temple mountain representing Mount Meru?
explanation: A Prasat is the sacred tower sanctuary symbolizing the cosmic peaks of Mount Meru.

text: Which Khmer festival honors ancestors and deceased relatives through food offerings at pagodas?
explanation: Pchum Ben is the 15-day religious festival dedicating merits to deceased ancestral spirits.

text: What famous hospital and medical ward system was established across the empire by Jayavarman VII?
explanation: Jayavarman VII constructed 102 Arogayasala medical clinics across the Khmer realm.

text: What water purification temple island was built by Jayavarman VII in the center of the Jayatataka Baray?
explanation: Neak Pean was a circular island temple sanctuary designed for sacred medical water purification.

text: What is the chemical symbol for the element Gold on the periodic table?
explanation: Au derives from the Latin word 'Aurum' meaning golden dawn.

text: What subatomic particles are located inside the nucleus of an atom?
explanation: The atomic nucleus contains positive protons and uncharged neutrons.

text: What is the pH value of a completely neutral aqueous solution at 25 degrees Celsius?
explanation: pH 7 represents exact neutrality, where hydrogen and hydroxide ions balance.

text: According to Ohm's Law in electrical circuits, how is Voltage (V) calculated?
explanation: Ohm's Law states Voltage equals Current (I) multiplied by Resistance (R).

text: What gas do living plants absorb from the atmosphere during the process of photosynthesis?
explanation: Photosynthesis consumes Carbon Dioxide and water to produce glucose and Oxygen.

text: What type of chemical reaction absorbs thermal energy from its surroundings, causing temperature to drop?
explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat energy from their environment.

text: What is the acceleration due to Earth's gravity near the surface (g)?
explanation: Standard Earth surface gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.806 m/s^2.

text: Which element is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere by volume?
explanation: Nitrogen comprises approximately 78.08% of Earth's atmosphere.

text: What law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another?
optionB: First Law of Thermodynamics (Conservation of Energy)
explanation: The First Law of Thermodynamics guarantees conservation of energy.

text: What is the chemical formula for ordinary table salt?
explanation: Sodium Chloride (NaCl) is common table salt.

text: What physical property describes a material's mass per unit volume?
explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume (rho = m / V).

text: What substance speeds up the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed itself?
explanation: Catalysts lower activation energy to accelerate chemical reactions.

text: What is the speed of light in a vacuum approximately?
explanation: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 299,792 km/s (3 x 10^8 m/s).

text: What type of bond is formed when two atoms share valence electrons?
explanation: Covalent bonding involves the mutual sharing of electron pairs.

text: Which state of matter consists of a superheated gas composed of free ions and unbound electrons?
explanation: Plasma is ionized gas with free electrons and positive ions.

text: What fundamental law of physics states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction?
explanation: Newton's Third Law dictates equal and opposite paired reaction forces.

text: What chemical compound has the chemical formula H2O2?
explanation: Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) is a strong oxidizer and antiseptic disinfectant.

text: What device converts mechanical kinetic motion into electrical energy via magnetic induction?
explanation: Generators induce electrical current by rotating coils through magnetic fields.

text: What is the temperature known as Absolute Zero on the Celsius scale?
explanation: Absolute zero is 0 Kelvin or -273.15 degrees Celsius.

text: Which acid is naturally found in automobile lead-acid storage batteries?
explanation: Sulfuric acid serves as the liquid electrolyte in lead-acid batteries.

text: What type of malware disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into executing it?
explanation: Trojan horses masquerade as benign files to breach computer systems.

text: What cyber attack involves injecting malicious SQL commands into database input fields?
explanation: SQLi exploits unsecured input to manipulate relational database queries.

text: Which cryptographic algorithm uses two separate mathematically linked keys: a public key and a private key?
explanation: Asymmetric encryption utilizes public keys for encryption and private keys for decryption.

text: What security attack overwhelms a web server with massive floods of artificial traffic from botnets?
explanation: DDoS attacks saturate target bandwidth and resources using distributed bots.

text: What does the 'S' stand for in the secure web protocol HTTPS?
explanation: HTTPS uses Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt web browser communications.

text: What is a Zero-Day vulnerability in software security?
optionA: A bug fixed on the day of release
optionB: A security flaw exploited in the wild before the vendor has developed a security patch
optionC: A virus that acts after 0 days
explanation: Zero-day vulnerabilities have no available patches at the time of exploitation.

text: What deceptive social engineering tactic uses fraudulent emails to steal credentials?
explanation: Phishing impersonates trustworthy organizations to deceive victims into revealing passwords.

text: Which hash function produces an unalterable 256-bit cryptographic digest?
explanation: SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit) is a cryptographic one-way hash function.

text: What security mechanism requires users to provide two or more distinct verification factors to authenticate?
explanation: MFA combines knowledge (password), possession (token/phone), or inherence (fingerprint).

text: What type of malware encrypts victim files and demands ransom payment in cryptocurrency for the decryption key?
explanation: Ransomware holds victim data hostage via strong encryption until ransom is paid.

text: What security tool monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic to block unauthorized packets based on rule sets?
explanation: Firewalls filter network traffic against defined security policy rules.

text: What attack occurs when a hacker intercepts and potentially alters communication between two unsuspecting parties?
explanation: MitM attacks eavesdrop or tamper with communication channels without detection.

text: What is a Honeypot in cyber defense architecture?
optionB: A deliberately vulnerable decoy system deployed to lure, detect, and analyze hacker techniques
explanation: Honeypots are decoy targets monitored to study attacker methods and gather threat intel.

text: What technique attempts every possible combination of characters until the correct password is found?
explanation: Brute force exhaustively guesses all character permutations to break passwords.

text: What attack executes malicious client-side scripts inside another user's web browser session?
explanation: XSS injects scripts into trusted web pages viewed by other users.

text: What is the principle of Least Privilege in system security?
optionA: Granting all users full administrator privileges
optionB: Users should be granted only the minimal levels of access necessary to perform their job duties
optionD: Only one user allowed per system
explanation: Least Privilege restricts user permissions to the bare minimum required.

text: What hidden program gives hackers persistent privileged administrator (root) access while concealing its presence?
explanation: Rootkits subvert operating system controls to conceal unauthorized administrative access.

text: What is a Salt in password storage and hashing?
optionB: Random data added to a password before hashing to defend against rainbow table attacks
explanation: Salting ensures identical passwords produce unique hash digests.

text: Which port is standard for HTTPS encrypted web traffic?
explanation: Port 443 is the standard port for TLS/SSL encrypted HTTPS traffic.

text: What cyber test simulates real-world hacker attacks against an organization with authorized permission?
explanation: Penetration testing evaluates defense posture through simulated ethical attacks.

text: What is the recommended ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths in standard adult CPR?
explanation: Standard adult CPR recommends 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.

text: What blood type is recognized as the universal red blood cell donor?
explanation: O Negative blood lacks A, B, and Rh antigens, making it universally tolerated.

text: What organ in the human body produces insulin to regulate blood glucose levels?
explanation: The endocrine pancreas produces insulin to facilitate cellular glucose uptake.

text: What is the primary function of white blood cells (leukocytes) in the body?
optionB: Defending against infections and foreign pathogens
explanation: Leukocytes constitute the immune system's cellular defense against infections.

text: What first aid procedure should immediately be administered for acute thermal burn injuries?
optionB: Cool the burn under cold running water for at least 10-20 minutes
optionD: Apply ice packs directly to skin
explanation: Cool clean running water dissipates heat and reduces tissue depth injury.

text: What is the largest organ in the human body by surface area and weight?
explanation: Human skin covers approximately 1.5 to 2 square meters.

text: What vital signs are assessed when checking a patient in critical triage?
optionB: Pulse, Respiration, Blood Pressure, and Temperature
explanation: Pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and core temperature are core vital signs.

text: What dangerous medical condition occurs when core body temperature drops below 35 degrees Celsius?
explanation: Hypothermia occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can generate it.

text: Which chambers of the human heart pump oxygen-rich blood out to the entire body?
explanation: The Left Ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta for systemic circulation.

text: What emergency device delivers an electric shock to restore a normal heart rhythm during cardiac arrest?
explanation: AEDs analyze cardiac arrhythmias and deliver defibrillating shocks if indicated.

text: What type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart under high pressure?
explanation: Arteries transport pressurized blood away from heart ventricles.

text: What is the standard normal resting body temperature for healthy humans in Celsius?
explanation: Average normal core body temperature is approximately 36.8 to 37.0 degrees Celsius.

text: What emergency maneuver is used to clear foreign body airway obstructions in choking victims?
explanation: The Heimlich maneuver uses upward abdominal thrusts to dislodge airway blockages.

text: What protein inside red blood cells binds to oxygen molecules for transport?
explanation: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing metalloprotein binding oxygen in erythrocytes.

text: What first aid technique should be applied immediately to control severe arterial bleeding?
optionB: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean sterile dressing
explanation: Firm direct pressure over the bleeding site stops most external hemorrhage.

text: What is the powerhouse organelle of eukaryotic cells responsible for producing ATP?
explanation: Mitochondria generate cellular chemical energy in the form of ATP.

text: Which vitamin is synthesized in human skin upon exposure to sunlight ultraviolet rays?
explanation: Vitamin D3 is synthesized in dermal layers upon UV-B radiation exposure.

text: What neurological cells transmit electrical impulses throughout the nervous system?
explanation: Neurons are specialized electrically excitable cells transmitting nerve impulses.

text: What physiological shock state results from catastrophic blood loss?
explanation: Hypovolemic shock results from acute loss of more than 20% of body fluid or blood.

text: What connective tissue connects skeletal muscles to bones?
explanation: Tendons anchor muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bone to bone.

text: What component is considered the primary 'brain' of a computer system?
explanation: The CPU executes instructions, arithmetic, and logical operations.

text: What is the primary difference between RAM and ROM memory?
optionA: RAM is permanent; ROM is temporary
optionB: RAM is volatile memory; ROM is non-volatile permanent memory
explanation: RAM loses contents when powered down (volatile); ROM permanently stores firmware.

text: Which storage technology uses flash memory chips with no moving mechanical parts?
explanation: SSDs utilize NAND flash memory chips for high-speed, shock-resistant storage.

text: What high-speed memory is located closest to the CPU cores to reduce memory access latency?
explanation: CPU Cache stores frequently referenced data directly adjacent to processor execution units.

text: What main circuit board connects all hardware components such as the CPU, RAM, and PCIe slots?
explanation: The motherboard provides physical sockets and electrical data buses between components.

text: What hardware component converts high-voltage alternating current (AC) into regulated low-voltage direct current (DC)?
explanation: The PSU converts household AC power into 12V, 5V, and 3.3V DC power rails.

text: What does ALU stand for in CPU microprocessor architecture?
explanation: The ALU performs integer arithmetic and bitwise logic operations in the CPU.

text: What does the CPU Clock Speed (measured in GHz) represent?
optionA: The amount of data in RAM
optionB: The number of electrical clock cycles executed per second
explanation: Clock frequency indicates how many billion execution cycles occur per second.

text: What firmware program initializes and tests computer hardware components during booting before loading the OS?
explanation: Basic Input/Output System (BIOS/UEFI) runs POST hardware validation during boot.

text: What expansion interface is standard for connecting modern graphics cards and NVMe storage?
explanation: PCIe provides high-bandwidth point-to-point serial communication lanes.

text: What is the function of thermal paste applied between the CPU heat spreader and cooler heatsink?
optionB: Fills microscopic air gaps to maximize heat transfer efficiency
explanation: Thermal compound eliminates insulating air pockets to conduct heat into the heatsink.

text: Which CPU architecture features thousands of small parallel cores optimized for graphics and matrix math?
explanation: GPUs feature massive parallel SIMD cores ideal for 3D geometry and matrix calculations.

text: What does NVMe stand for in modern ultra-fast solid state storage drives?
explanation: NVMe operates directly over PCIe lanes to provide massive read/write throughput.

text: What is CPU throttling?
optionB: Automatically reducing CPU clock speed to prevent overheating or save battery power
explanation: Thermal throttling drops clock frequency when temperature limits are reached.

text: What hardware register inside the CPU holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?
explanation: The Program Counter tracks the memory location of the next machine instruction.

text: How many bits are in one standard computer byte?
explanation: One byte consists of exactly 8 binary bits (an octet).

text: What is overclocking in computer hardware performance tuning?
optionA: Running a component at higher clock speed than its factory rating
explanation: Overclocking boosts clock frequency beyond factory specifications for higher performance.

text: Which hardware component prevents power surge damage from lightning and voltage spikes?
explanation: Surge protectors and Uninterruptible Power Supplies shield against electrical spikes.

text: What does RAID 1 configuration provide in hard drive storage arrays?
optionB: Disk Mirroring (identical data duplicate on two drives for redundancy)
explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives to survive single disk failure.

text: What is the primary function of the CMOS battery on a computer motherboard?
optionB: Maintaining real-time clock (RTC) and BIOS settings when unplugged
explanation: The CR2032 CMOS battery powers the real-time clock and volatile firmware memory.

text: In Boolean logic, what is the output of an AND gate if input A is 1 (True) and input B is 0 (False)?
explanation: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1.

text: Which logic gate outputs 1 (True) only when its two binary inputs are different?
explanation: XOR outputs 1 if inputs differ (0,1 or 1,0); 0 if identical.

text: What is the binary representation of the decimal number 13?
explanation: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, which corresponds to binary 1101.

text: According to De Morgan's Laws, what is equivalent to NOT (A AND B)?
explanation: De Morgan's first theorem states !(A & B) = !A | !B.

text: According to De Morgan's Laws, what is equivalent to NOT (A OR B)?
explanation: De Morgan's second theorem states !(A | B) = !A & !B.

text: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of the decimal number 255?
explanation: 255 in hexadecimal is FF (15*16 + 15).

text: What logic gate produces an output that is the exact inverse of an AND gate?
explanation: NAND (Not AND) inverts the output of an AND gate.

text: What is the logical converse of the conditional statement 'If P, then Q'?
optionA: If not P, then not Q
optionC: If not Q, then not P
explanation: The converse of 'P -> Q' is 'Q -> P'.

text: Which statement is logically equivalent to the conditional proposition 'If P, then Q'?
optionB: Contrapositive (If not Q, then not P)
optionC: Inverse (If not P, then not Q)
explanation: A conditional statement is logically equivalent only to its contrapositive.

text: In set theory, what is the set containing elements that belong to Set A OR Set B called?
explanation: The Union of two sets contains all elements belonging to either set.

text: How many unique rows are in the truth table for a Boolean function with 4 binary input variables?
explanation: A truth table with n binary variables has 2^n rows; 2^4 = 16 rows.

text: What is the result of the bitwise operation: 1010 AND 1100 in binary?
explanation: Bitwise AND compares paired bits: 1&1=1, 0&1=0, 1&0=0, 0&0=0 -> 1000.

text: What is the result of the bitwise operation: 0101 XOR 0011 in binary?
What is a tautology in formal logic?
optionA: A statement that is always false
optionB: A statement that is true in every possible interpretation
explanation: A tautology is a compound proposition that evaluates to True for all truth values.

text: What is the decimal value of the binary number 10000000 (2^7)?
explanation: 1 followed by seven zeros in binary represents 2^7 = 128.

text: In Boolean algebra, what is the value of (A OR 1) regardless of the truth value of A?
explanation: The Dominance Law dictates A OR 1 = 1.

text: In Boolean algebra, what is the value of (A AND 0) regardless of the truth value of A?
explanation: The Annihilator/Dominance Law dictates A AND 0 = 0.

text: What graphical diagram is used by electrical engineers to simplify Boolean algebra expressions?
explanation: Karnaugh maps visually group adjacent minterms to minimize logic expressions.

text: What is a contradiction in propositional logic?
optionB: A statement that evaluates to False in all possible truth assignments
explanation: A contradiction is universally false under all interpretations.

text: If all Students study, and Dara is a Student, what valid deductive conclusion follows?
explanation: Modus Ponens deduction confirms Dara studies.

text: What core software program acts as the central interface between computer hardware and user applications?
explanation: The Kernel is the core component managing CPU, memory, and hardware I/O.

text: What memory management technique uses secondary disk storage to simulate additional physical RAM?
explanation: Virtual memory pages inactive memory blocks to disk swap space.

text: What deadlock condition occurs when a process holds resources while requesting additional locked resources?
explanation: Hold and Wait occurs when processes hold existing allocations while waiting for more.

text: What is the primary difference between a process and a thread in modern operating systems?
optionA: Processes share memory, threads do not
optionB: A process is an isolated executing program; threads are lightweight execution units within a process sharing memory
explanation: Threads share the parent process's memory space, open files, and global state.

text: What CPU scheduling algorithm executes tasks in the exact order they arrive in the ready queue?
explanation: FCFS dispatches processes non-preemptively based strictly on queue arrival time.

text: What mechanism allows hardware devices to signal the CPU immediately that an event requires attention?
explanation: Interrupts cause the CPU to pause current tasks and invoke an Interrupt Service Routine.

text: What is a Context Switch in multi-tasking operating systems?
optionB: Saving the state of a running process and restoring another to share the CPU
explanation: Context switching saves and restores CPU registers so multiple tasks share execution time.

text: What system call is used in Unix/Linux operating systems to spawn a new child process?
explanation: fork() creates an exact duplicate child process with unique PID.

text: What synchronization variable or primitive protects critical sections by signaling integer permits?
explanation: Counting semaphores maintain integer permits to control access to shared resources.

text: What dangerous operating system phenomenon occurs when excessive paging starves CPU execution?
explanation: Thrashing occurs when the OS spends more time swapping virtual pages than executing code.

text: What command line utility in Linux displays real-time CPU, memory, and running process utilization?
explanation: top/htop provides interactive real-time process monitoring.

text: Which open-source operating system kernel was created in 1991 by Linus Torvalds?
explanation: Linus Torvalds released the initial Linux kernel in 1991.

text: What file system is the default standard for modern Microsoft Windows installations?
explanation: New Technology File System (NTFS) is standard on Windows.

text: What is the root administrative superuser account called in Unix and Linux operating systems?
explanation: 'root' is the superuser account possessing unrestricted system permissions in Unix.

text: What CPU scheduling algorithm allocates a fixed slice of CPU time (time quantum) to each process in turn?
explanation: Round Robin cycles through processes granting each a fixed time slice.

text: What signal in Unix systems forces immediate, non-catchable process termination?
explanation: SIGKILL (9) cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored by the target process.

text: What is a Race Condition in concurrent multithreaded programming?
optionA: Two threads competing to run faster
optionB: Flawed behavior occurring when program output depends on the uncontrollable timing of thread execution
explanation: Race conditions emerge when shared state is modified without proper synchronization.

text: What memory segmentation divides physical memory into fixed-size contiguous blocks called frames?
explanation: Paging maps fixed-size logical pages to physical memory frames.

text: Which command changes directory locations in both Windows PowerShell and Linux bash terminals?
explanation: 'cd' changes the current working directory across command shells.

text: What file permission in Linux allows reading, writing, and executing for the file owner (binary 111)?
explanation: Read (4) + Write (2) + Execute (1) = Octal 7.
